title: Comunicado 2025-12-18
summary: Banxico cut the policy rate 25bp to 7.00% by a 4-1 majority, with Heath dissenting for a hold at 7.25%, judging it appropriate to continue the easing cycle given the peso, weak activity and trade-policy risks and taking into account the restriction already implemented. The main change versus the 6 November communique is the forward guidance: the explicit 'valorará recortar la tasa de referencia' gives way to 'valorará el momento de realizar ajustes adicionales', dropping the word cut and putting the emphasis on timing, which reads as a signal that a pause is near. The inflation backdrop also worsened: headline and core rose, and the headline and core forecasts were revised up for Q4 2025 and the next two quarters on a slower decline in services, although convergence to 3% is still expected in Q3 2026. The balance of risks stays tilted up (less than in 2021-2024), with the IEPS and tariff changes flagged as a transitory upside that may later be built into the forecast. Net, still a cut, but with de-committed guidance pointing to a slower pace and a persistent hawkish dissent, so it sits at the cautious end of the easing phase.

key_quotes.quote: La Junta de Gobierno juzgó apropiado continuar con el ciclo de disminuciones de la tasa de referencia.
key_quotes.context: Fifth consecutive 25bp cut, to 7.00%, framed as continuing the cycle

key_quotes.quote: Hacia delante, la Junta de Gobierno valorará el momento de realizar ajustes adicionales a la tasa de referencia.
key_quotes.context: Guidance shifts from 'valorará recortar' (November) to assessing the timing of further adjustments: a pause signal

key_quotes.quote: Los pronósticos de las inflaciones general y subyacente se ajustaron al alza para el cuarto trimestre de 2025 y los siguientes dos.
key_quotes.context: Forecasts revised up on slower services disinflation

key_quotes.quote: Votó a favor de mantener el objetivo para la Tasa de Interés Interbancaria a un día en un nivel de 7.25% Jonathan Heath.
key_quotes.context: Heath dissents again for a hold
